cultural.vision_reason: A narrow-strip woven cotton cloth with geometric supplementary-weft diamond patterning, consistent with Papel men's/women's wrap garments from Guinea-Bissau; strip-woven textiles of this type are characteristic of the region's peoples.

physical.title: garment
physical.summary:
Textile, garment (worn by men and women) made of cotton. Narrow strip woven cotton cloth consisting of 6 strips sewn loosely together selvedge to selvedge. Plain weave: white and dyed black warps and wefts. Textile can be split into three decorative bands. The central band consists of a black and white square grid: each segment of the grid is decorated with five diamonds, a large central diamond with a small diamond in each corner, in dyed black cotton in supplementary weft. The two bands, one at either end of the textile, which consist of:
* Ground weave: white background with black warp stripes that are crossed in the weft direction at the edge of the textile.
* Supplementary weave: there are two decorative bands in dyed black cotton based around zigzags and diamond shapes.

The textile is finished by unworked warps.
